title: Expected acceptance of a random three-literal clause
statement: Let $\sigma$ assign a Boolean choice to each of three positions, and let $v=(v_0,v_1,v_2)$ be a triple of signs in $\{\pm1\}$. Choose $b$ uniformly from $\{\pm1\}$ and form the clause whose falsifying signs are $(1,b,b)$, negating the sign at each position where $\sigma$ is true. The expected acceptance indicator of this clause on $v$ is $\frac12$ plus half the acceptance indicator of the triple obtained by negating the inputs according to $\sigma$ for the predicate that accepts $(x_0,x_1,x_2)$ exactly when $x_0\ne 1$ or $x_1\ne x_2$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean choice for each of three positions
